thread:
taylor: Kicking off v3.0.1 in change window (USW). Canary 15% now. Noticed slight throughput drop on dedicated embeddings routes.
rui: saw the deploybot note. numbers?
deploybot: ALERT: canary throughput -12% vs baseline (3m). Auto-rollback criteria: throughput drop >=20% OR error rate >=1% sustained 5m. Current: -12% (3m), errors 0.04%.
ops-oncall: Not hitting auto threshold yet but given change window and some reserved customers, i'd prefer to pin and evaluate. Manual-rollback authority: oncall if degradation >=15% for 5m or customer impact.
taylor: I'll apply a manual hold and open a quick investigation. If we decide to rollback, we should pin to 2.9.8 for dedicated pools only to avoid global churn.
deploybot: ACTION: canary hold applied by taylor. Traffic frozen at 15%. Auto-rollback still active.
docs_cam: Heads-up: release notes still reference quantization improvements; please add a blurb noting possible perf variance across hardware. I'll draft.
rui: Running a short perf probe across the dedicated pool (10m). If degradation persists and offline tests reproduce, recommend rollback to 2.9.8 and a rollback comms blurb.
(8m later)
rui: probe shows sustained -16% throughput (10m window) on dedicated-A (NVLink). Offline repro on staging with same kernel flags.
taylor: Given the repro and reserved customers in region, approving manual rollback for dedicated pools. Command: `/deploy rollback --to 2.9.8 --scope=dedicated-pool-A --region=usw`
deploybot: ROLLBACK STARTED by taylor. Graceful drain queued; estimated 4m to restore pool.
ops-oncall: Preparing customer note and release-note amendment. docs_cam, please include exact rollback reason: quantization kernel interaction on NVLink causing throughput regressions.
docs_cam: Draft ready, pushing to releases repo and will notify growth for customer-facing blurb.
deploybot: ROLLBACK COMPLETE. Dedicated pool A reverted to 2.9.8. Canary traffic replaced with fallback variant.
rui: Post-rollback metrics: throughput back to baseline, errors unchanged. Closing hold.
taylor: Filing a short postmortem and pinging kernel team for a follow-up fix. Also leaving a note in the release thread explaining selective dedicated rollback to avoid global revert.
ops-oncall: Good runbook execution. Marking incident as minor and assigning follow-up actions.
